raw_response:
I will do this year much like I do in a normal year, just a little tighter on money and labor. My farm is only 7 mu, and some people in my house work outside, so I will not put too much land into cotton because cotton needs more watching and more spraying. I will keep most of the land in wheat-maize because that is the steady way here and I have well water, so I can still push yield if the rain is short. I will follow what works on the nearby fields: good wheat seed, hybrid maize, and not let fertilizer get too low. If I am unsure, I would rather put a bit more fertilizer than watch the crop turn weak. For wheat I will feed it heavier because wheat needs strong tillers and full heads. For maize I will still feed it well after wheat, but I will watch costs because there is already fertilizer left in the ground. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece, give it enough base fertilizer and more spraying, because if insects get ahead, cotton is hard to save.
